title: Cyclic length and chromatic fixed-point loss
coverage: Read all of sections 1–7 in the LaTeX source and checked every step of the lower-bound chain. (1) Prop 3.2 occurrence closure: the Sylow-unit argument, subgroup closure through the norm map and Φ^L N_I^L ≃ Φ^I, and the elementary-abelian bound through ADLM/BHNNNS sharpness plus the cofree projection formula. (2) Thm 3.3 maximizing tower: monotonicity of conjugacy-class counts, the Goursat/graph classification of the surviving summands, and r_α/s_α/t_α with t r = |C_F(α L)|. I checked the normalizer index by hand. (3) Integration weights from Δ_!1 and the module identity. (4) Scalar integrality: 1+px is a unit via p^2 id_M = 0 and M-locality of T(l)-local spectra. (5) Subgroup congruences: coinduced labeled-set groupoids, the Shapiro-type identification of the homotopy fiber with L_j(X), the integral equality of point restrictions, and the exponential/log formula with pointed transitive objects. I spot-checked these: for Γ=Z_p the generating function is Artin–Hasse (p-integral); the congruence holds for Z_p and for transitive Z_p^2-sets, using a_h(2)−a_{h−w}(2) having valuation h−w+1. (6) Profinite theorem: the shrinking-action lemma (the kernel of E_s→Q_M is generated by the pieces that every map to Σ_M kills; index bounds), Goursat count c_h, lattice-count limit c_d (a p-adic unit), the Frattini detector, and termination through the section bound. (7) Product-series compactness lemma and the rank-increment argument. (8) Height gluing: ring nilpotence (HS Thm 3), B=L_K(E∧R) is nonzero, full-mark trace N_{k,r}=|GL_k(Z/p^r)| (the rank p^{rk^2} matches the character count), and trace preservation under base change. (9) Finite gluing induction over the fracture square, including the module-retraction step for the overlap corner. (10) Section 7: layer right adjoints and the fixed-point formula, both orthogonality conditions (the chain-concatenation inequality m<k+d), the stripping induction in the splitting lemma, the construction of a compact object with support exactly Z, and the irreducibility contradiction; then the deduction of Thm 1.1 from prime inclusions. The intro example and the general-group corollary are also consistent. One citation not verified: CSY Theorem 4.3.5 (torsion-nilpotence), used in Lemma 6.2. I believe the statement is true and did not count it as a gap. I did not independently verify Lemma 6.4 (the genuine-equivariant model for the product comparison) beyond its plausibility as a standard construction.
main_claim: For every prime p, finite p-group G, subgroup H and height n≥0, the chromatic fixed-point loss r_n(G,H) equals ℓ(G,H), the minimal length of a cyclic-quotient subnormal chain from H to G. This answers Kuhn–Lloyd's question, including height independence. The proof works as follows. Rational nonvanishing of U_P(L_{T(l)}S) produces a pro-p group Γ↠P whose finite sections have rank ≤ l. Γ also satisfies Hom-count integrality and the subgroup congruences, and these force a poly-Z_p series of length ≤ l. The result is lifted to all heights via HKR full-mark traces, and the support-splitting argument then gives the specialization bound.
sibling_notes: The family 314 board was empty when I started. Results here that companion papers may reuse: the profinite theorem (section rank ≤ l + Hom integrality + subgroup congruences ⇒ poly-Z_p of length ≤ l), and the labeled-set congruence Σ_{[U:V]=p^h}(|X^V|−|X|) ∈ p^{h+1}Z_(p).
